A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with the same title, authors, and core experiments. Their text, equations, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including material relocated between sections.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic SAE experiments, Gemma and Llama sparse-probing evaluations, and an analysis of reported L0 values for open-source SAEs.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds correlation and L0 sensitivity experiments, superposition experiments, and Gemma-2-2b layer 20 evaluations.

M1.justification: The SAE architectures, losses, and automatic L0-adjustment procedure are retained. Decoder pairwise cosine similarity, foregrounded in v3, already appears with the same definition in v2 Appendix A.5; nth decoder projection remains available in v3 Appendix A.9. This changes emphasis rather than introducing a new algorithm.

E1.justification: v3 adds synthetic input scenarios with overlapping features in Appendices A.3.3 and A.4.1, extending the orthogonal toy settings retained from v2. These include 50 features represented in 40 dimensions. The Pile and sparse-probing task collection remain unchanged; the additional LLM layer is a model-setting extension.

E2.justification: v2 Figure 15 includes a BatchTopK-versus-JumpReLU comparison for k=1 probing on Gemma-2-2b layer 12 that v3 omits. Their k=16 comparison and the trained-versus-ground-truth toy comparisons remain. MDL-SAEs and AFA-SAEs are newly discussed but are not evaluated as baselines.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce correlation sweeps from -0.5 to 0.5, small-model L0 sweeps from 1.7 to 2.0, L0=1.9 for the small superposition experiment, and evaluation at Gemma-2-2b layer 20. Existing experiments retain their reported training budgets and settings. These are extensions of the evaluation design, not evidence that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 Appendices A.3–A.4 substantially expand controlled validation: they test how mixing changes with correlation strength and L0 shortfall, and whether mixing and the cosine metric persist under superposition noise. v2 lacks these systematic analyses. The earlier L0-transition and encoder-bias/threshold analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report five seeds for the established toy sweeps, three seeds per L0 for the main LLM sweeps, and standard-deviation shading. Added results continue these reporting practices, including five seeds for the large superposition experiment. No increased run count, new confidence-interval practice, or significance testing is reported.

E6.justification: v3 adds sensitivity, superposition, JumpReLU cosine-metric, and layer 20 probing results. The layer 12 cosine curves also change: v2 Figure 15 shows similar high-L0 values for BatchTopK and JumpReLU, whereas v3 Figure 9 shows substantially higher BatchTopK values. The layer 12 k=1 results are removed. Figure 5 changes its middle example from L0=2 to L0=5, although the accompanying paragraph still says L0=2.

T1.justification: v3 adds three formal arguments absent from v2: a two-feature MSE analysis of low-L0 mixing, a shared-component proof for increased pairwise cosine similarity, and a Gaussian projection/quantile argument for nth decoder projection. Appendices A.5, A.6, and A.10 introduce substantial assumptions, derivations, and theorem statements beyond the retained metric definitions.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the central claims: incorrect L0 produces mixed features, reconstruction tradeoffs can favor incorrect dictionaries, proxy metrics can guide L0 selection, and commonly used SAEs often have excessively low L0. The additional evidence supports these existing claims rather than redefining their scope.

C2.justification: v3 replaces v2's lack of a strong metric preference with a preference for cosine similarity because it is simpler and has no hyperparameters. It omits the earlier interpretation connecting the metrics' different alignment with k=1 versus k=16 probing to latent heterogeneity, and emphasizes broad flat regions as a metric limitation. The dedicated limitations section is otherwise retained.

D1.justification: v3 Appendix A.17 adds PyTorch pseudocode for both metrics, making normalization, pair selection, projection sorting, and indexing explicit. The new experiments also receive parameter descriptions. Existing training-detail sections and the code-access URL are retained; no new hardware or runtime information is supplied.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds focused positioning against MDL-SAEs by Ayonrinde et al. and AFA-SAEs by Lee et al., contrasting their approaches to choosing SAE hyperparameters with the paper's ground-truth-feature perspective. Templeton et al. is also added for feature-splitting context. The existing feature-hedging positioning remains.

P1.justification: The central exposition is reorganized around cosine similarity: v2's alternative-metric appendix becomes the basis of v3 Section 3.5 and the main empirical narrative, while projection-metric exposition moves into Appendix A.9. Related work gains thematic subsections, and the appendix is substantially reorganized around experiments, theory, and implementation. The opening sections remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: The main and appendix metric figures exchange roles, several composite figures are rebuilt, and the layer 12 k=1 panel is removed. v3 adds correlation/L0 sensitivity plots, superposition heatmaps and curves, a layer 20 figure, and two pseudocode figures. These are substantial display changes beyond renumbering and page reflow.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens validation through controlled sensitivity tests, overlapping-feature experiments, and a later LLM layer, while metric pseudocode improves reproducibility. The new theory makes restricted supporting arguments explicit but does not establish general guarantees for the proxies. These gains improve support for the existing conclusions, tempered by removal of the informative layer 12 k=1 comparison and the newly inconsistent Figure 5 labeling and discussion.
